title: What MeshOptimiser is
summary: A free app that runs on your own computer. It turns a heavy CAD file into a light 3D file and lets you inspect, clean up and export it.

title: Words you will meet
summary: A plain-language glossary: STEP, mesh, triangle, GLB, instancing, decimation, WebGPU, virtual environment and the other terms these pages use.

title: Open your first file
summary: Drop a file on the window. What the import settings mean, what conversion does, how to follow its progress, and where the result is kept.

title: Native CAD files: export a STEP file first
groupTitle: Getting your model out of your CAD program
summary: MeshOptimiser opens STEP, not SolidWorks, Inventor, Creo or CATIA files. Why, which STEP version to pick, and where to find the steps for your program.

title: How to export a STEP assembly from Autodesk Inventor
groupTitle: Getting your model out of your CAD program
summary: Save an Inventor assembly as one STEP file with Save Copy As, pick AP214, and learn what Shrinkwrap can do for a very large assembly.

title: How to export a STEP assembly from Onshape
groupTitle: Getting your model out of your CAD program
summary: Export an Onshape assembly or Part Studio as STEP by right-clicking its tab, and why STEP is a better start than Onshape’s own glTF export.

title: How to export a STEP assembly from PTC Creo
groupTitle: Getting your model out of your CAD program
summary: Save a Creo assembly as one STEP file with Save a Copy, set the application protocol and keep Export assembly as on Single File.

title: How to export a STEP file from Rhino
groupTitle: Getting your model out of your CAD program
summary: Export selected Rhino objects as STEP with File, Export Selected: which protocol keeps colours, what happens to black objects, and what to do with meshes.

title: The window
summary: A tour of the screen: the top bar and tabs, the parts tree, the 3D view and its toolbars, the cards on the right, the drawers, the status bar and how to resize it all.

title: Move the view
summary: Orbit, pan and zoom with the mouse, frame a part with F, and switch between the camera, Top, Front and Side views.

title: Select parts
summary: Click, add with Shift, toggle with Ctrl, drag a box, or let the app select by shape, colour or name.

title: Hide, isolate, show all
summary: Hide parts that are in the way, look at a few parts on their own, and bring everything back with one key.

title: The parts tree
summary: Search, rename, group and reorder the parts of a model, rename many at once, and flatten a hierarchy that is deeper than you need.

title: Organise the tree: groups, sorting and picking
summary: Pick groups and parts together, take a group out of the tree without losing what is in it, flatten, sort and move groups.

title: Search and commands
summary: Press Ctrl + K or Shift + C to find any command, part, library part or setting by name, turn a switch without leaving the list, and work out a sum or convert a length.

title: Quick wand
summary: Hold W and a ring of commands opens under the pointer. Flick toward one and let go.

title: Undo and redo
summary: Every editing action can be taken back with Ctrl + Z. What counts as one step, and how to go back to the file as it was opened.

title: Scene tabs
summary: Each tab is a scene of its own. Open several files side by side, drop a file to add it or open it in a tab, drag tabs into order, and save from the tab’s dot.

title: Settings
summary: One window with its sections and a search. What each section holds, in a sentence or two, from the start-up options and the search to the look of the interface.

title: How to read the numbers
summary: What a triangle count tells you, where the app shows it, how to find the heaviest parts, and how to see what your work has saved.

title: Heavy parts
summary: A list of the parts that hold the most triangles, heaviest first, with a count beside its title. Tick the ones you do not need and delete them in one step.

title: Smart optimise
summary: One card, one button: every clean-up the app has, run one after another on the whole scene. Choose how far to go, read the plan, press Optimise.

title: Delete small parts
summary: Remove the screws, washers and clips that are too small to matter, with a slider and a preview of what will go.

title: Select hidden parts
summary: Find every part that cannot be seen from outside the model, such as screws inside a housing, and delete them in one step.

title: Fasteners
summary: Find every bolt, screw, nut and washer by its shape, whatever the parts are called, then isolate or delete them in one step.

title: Stacked copies
summary: Find parts that sit exactly on top of an identical copy of themselves, drawn twice, and remove the extra ones.

title: Remove holes
summary: Close bolt holes, slots, pockets and lettering in flat faces. Each closed hole removes the triangles of its walls.

title: Remove floating pieces
summary: Delete the small loose pieces of a part that touch nothing: a plug, a shaving, a dot of a thread. The biggest piece of each part always stays.

title: Remesh: Untriangulate and Triangulate
summary: Join the triangles of each flat face into one polygon and take away the vertices in its middle, or go back to even triangles. The shape stays as it is.

title: Split
summary: Take apart a mesh that arrived as one piece but is really several separate solids, or cut it into its faces, so each can be selected on its own.

title: Smart fit
summary: Replace a detailed part with a simple stand-in of the same size and position: a box, a cylinder, a few boxes, or blocks that keep its outline.

title: Decimate
summary: Remove a share of the triangles from the selected parts while keeping their shape. Choose a percentage or a target, and preview first.

title: Fit to budget
summary: Type the number of triangles the whole scene may have. The densest meshes are reduced first until the total fits.

title: Quick fixes and tidying up
summary: Small one-click repairs: remove empty parts and empty groups, fix shading, recentre the model and make moves permanent.

title: A sensible order to work in
summary: A suggested routine for a first clean-up: look, delete what is not needed, simplify what remains, check, save and export.

title: View modes
summary: Six ways to draw the same model: solid, wireframe, X-ray, heatmap, clay and CAD. One key each, plus the Shading card for the clay and CAD looks.

title: Colours and materials
summary: Open the materials dock to see every material in the scene, recolour all the parts that share one, assign a material with a button or by dragging it onto a part, and let the dock float as a window.

title: Move, rotate, scale and measure
summary: Use the gizmo to move, turn and resize parts, drag a part over other surfaces with Dynamic place, type exact values in the transform card, and measure the distance between two points.

title: Edit mesh: points, edges and polygons
summary: Pick and change the pieces a part is made of: its points, edges and polygons. Move, delete, dissolve, planarize, straighten, weld, fill and extract them, from a bar at the right of the view.

title: Align to floor
summary: Stand a model upright on the grid, centred over the origin, when it arrived on its side or far away from the centre of the scene. A small drawing shows the result first.

title: Align parts
summary: Line the selected parts up along an axis, or space them evenly, with one press. Each press is one undo step.

title: Exploded view
summary: Push the parts of an assembly apart with one slider, choose the directions, and put them back with one click.

title: The parts library and shapes
summary: Add standard parts to a scene from a drawer under the viewport: 112 bolts, nuts, pipes, profiles, machine parts, electronics and brackets. Look at a part and set its size before it goes in.

title: Draw lines and shapes
summary: Draw curves, rectangles, circles and polygons on the floor or on a face, edit their points, and use them as paths.

title: Sweep a profile along a line
summary: Turn a path and a profile into a solid part: a pipe, a rail, a ring.

title: Screenshots
summary: Save a picture of the viewport as a PNG, at the size of the view or at any resolution up to poster size.

title: Save a scene
summary: Save your work as a scene file so you can carry on later. What a scene file is, how to name it with the file-name buttons, and how it differs from an export.

title: Get your scene back after a crash
summary: While a scene has changes that are not saved, a copy is kept inside your browser. If the app crashes, it offers the scene back the next time it starts.

title: Export
summary: Write the model to GLB, glTF, FBX, USDZ, OBJ, STL, PLY or a parts list, name the file, and set the scale, up axis and origin the next program needs.

title: Which format should I choose
summary: A short guide by purpose: the web, Cinema 4D, Blender, game engines, AR on an iPhone, 3D printing, or a parts list.

title: How to convert a STEP file to GLB
summary: Convert a STEP CAD file to a small GLB for the web, on your own computer and for free. The model is never uploaded. Drop it in, check it, export.

title: How to remove bolts and screws from a STEP assembly
summary: Take the bolts, screws, nuts and washers out of a CAD assembly before it goes on the web. Select one, select the rest, check, delete, and undo if needed.

title: How to make a CAD model safe to send to a customer
summary: Show your product without handing over your design. Remove hidden parts and fasteners, simplify what is left, clean the names and export a small GLB.

title: Keyboard shortcuts
summary: Every keyboard shortcut and mouse action in MeshOptimiser v0.24.0, grouped by what it does.

title: File formats
summary: Which files the app opens and which it writes, and what each format keeps: the parts tree, materials and vertex colours.

title: Privacy and offline use
summary: MeshOptimiser runs on your own computer. What stays local, when the internet is used, and what the browser remembers.

title: Troubleshooting
summary: Fixes for the usual problems: Python not found, a blocked launcher on macOS, missing modules, a blank view and slow conversions.

title: Frequently asked questions
summary: Short answers: cost and licence, privacy, browsers, file sizes, whether Python is needed, and where to report a bug.
